cover_letter.greeting: Dear AWS Data Center Finance Team,
paragraphs: I'm applying for the Finance Manager, Data Center Planning and Delivery role at AWS. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. Data center buildout is the part of the AI economy I most want to work on, and a seat that follows capital from planning through construction and commissioning is where the real cost and timing decisions get made.

At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%, and ran variance and sensitivity analyses on budget changes for cross-functional teams. For an MBA project I modeled a 6-project, 35.4 MW Illinois solar portfolio, covering capital structure, DSCR, NPV and levered IRR, which taught me how build costs, incentives and timing flow into returns on physical infrastructure. At Thomson Reuters I supported monthly P&L forecasting, variance analysis and close for the ANZ region.

That maps to the forecasting, financial controls and capital tracking the role describes. I haven't worked in construction finance, so I'd start by learning how AWS plans and tracks a data center build. I'm careful with data, quick to find where a number went wrong, and comfortable explaining it to non-finance partners. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
